claim: Unconstrained stochastic hill-climbing on the step heights, starting from the constant, raises R well above the 2/3 seed: multi-scale block perturbations with restarts and coordinate polish reached 0.7239 at N=300 (p0006), and smooth-perturbation hill-climb with resampling reached 0.8329 at N=50 (p0002). The gain comes from breaking the triangle's sharp peak: the winning shapes have a flatter, bro

Structured nonconstant shapes already beat the constant without any local search: edge-heavy/concave-up families reached 0.7086 (p0003) and a symmetric trapezoid with a central plateau and tapered edges reached 0.7238 (p0005), both at N=2000. The trapezoid result shows a flat central plateau with lowered edges is a genuinely good shape, consistent with flattening the convolution top rather than co

The best shapes share a common signature: f*f is made flatter and broader (more knots near its maximum) and its peak is pushed off-center, which lowers ||f*f||_inf faster than it lowers ||f*f||_2^2. The constant's triangle is the worst case for this ratio; every improvement found (p0002, p0004, p0005, p0006) moves in this direction, and the highest scorers (p0002 at 0.833, p0004 at 0.807) have the

Resolution and search method trade off: the best score came at coarse N=50 (p0002, 0.833) while finer N=800-4000 hill-climbs plateaued lower (p0004 0.807, p0007 0.804). It is unclear whether coarse discretization itself helps (fewer degrees of freedom, smoother f*f) or whether the finer searches were simply less effective per unit budget; testing the same hill-climb at matched effective resolution

Systematic coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps (multi-epsilon, accept-immediately) plus block-perturbation escapes and periodic multi-resolution kicks beat p0002's random-only block hill-climb on the same N=50 shape: 0.8329 -> 0.8523 (p0010). The gain comes from exploiting the existing coarse shape more thoroughly rather than searching a new one, confirming there was real headroom left at N=50.

A monotone gamma-warp of p0002's profile (area-averaging over warped knots) followed by the base block climb reached 0.8553 (p0008), the best of generation 2, from 0.8329. The warp stage acts as a real mechanism for reshaping the profile, not just a search kick; the winning shape ended with a centered f*f peak (0.50) and 14% zeros, so the earlier off-center peak was incidental rather than causal.

Finer-resolution climbs from p0002 itself (p0012 at N=200 -> 0.8497; p0009 at N=32000 -> 0.8391; p0011 at N=3200 -> 0.8432; p0013 at N=800 -> 0.8372) all landed below the N=50 coordinate search (p0010, 0.8523) and the N=50 warp (p0008, 0.8553). This is consistent with coarse N being advantageous, but each fine run used a different search method and budget, so whether N=50 is intrinsically special

A low-dimensional control-point representation (K=8-16 control values linearly interpolated to the step heights, optimized by Nelder-Mead with restarts, then block-perturbation polish) escapes the N=50 local basin that all local moves from p0008 keep returning to: from p0008 (0.8553) it reached 0.8597 (p0017), a +0.0044 gain, producing a smooth zero-free shape (0% zeros, max/mean 3.62) at N=200 wi

Progressive N escalation with area-average resampling plus a final extend stage of short restarts from the best-so-far, all sharing one global best, gave the generation's top score: from p0008 (0.8553) it reached 0.8669 (p0014) at N=400, a +0.0116 gain, with the f*f peak pushed strongly off-center (0.286). This shows that finer resolution does help when the search method is held fixed and the budg

Combining the two separately-proven operators on the same shape — alternating gamma-warp sweeps with coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps and short block-perturbation escapes at N=50 — beats either alone: from p0008 (0.8553) it reached 0.8637 (p0019), a +0.0084 gain, confirming the warp and coordinate-sweep gains are complementary rather than redundant.

A controlled resolution sweep using the identical warp-then-block-climb method at each N (30-200) from p0008 returned its start unchanged after 22 s of a 25 s budget (p0018), so it is not evidence about whether N=50 is intrinsically special; the equal-slice budget left too little time per N for the change to act. It needs a larger budget or fewer N values to settle the question.

Running the strong operator engine (gamma-warp sweep + coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps + block escapes) inside a resolution escalation, rather than the plain random block climb used before, lifts the frontier: from p0014 (0.8669, N=400) it reached 0.8761 at N=800 (+0.0093), the best score so far. The gain comes from the strong engine acting at each escalation level, so the coarse-N local str

Coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps at increasing resolution (400->1400) with periodic restarts from best, using a fast local score for small perturbations, beat random block perturbations on p0014's state: 0.8669 -> 0.8707 (+0.0038) at N=1400. The local score makes each coordinate test cheap enough to sweep the whole array many times, so local structure is exploited far more thoroughly than ran

Whether an explicit monotone exponential tilt of f (pushing f*f's peak further off-centre than p0014's 0.286) raises R is still unsettled: the tilt+polish program on p0014 returned its start unchanged after 32 s of a 35 s budget, so it is not evidence about the tilt idea. It needs a longer budget or a cheaper tilt-only probe to decide.

Replacing a fixed one-pass resolution escalation with repeated perturb-then-engine restarts from the global best, cycling N over coarse-to-mid values and forcing the finest N in the last fifth of the budget, lifts the frontier: from p0021 (0.876128, N=800) it reached 0.878330 (p0026), the generation's top score. The gain comes from spending the whole budget on many short restarts rather than one e

Whether resolution beyond N=800 is a live lever for the smooth winning profile is still unsettled: a clean probe upsampling p0021 to N=1600/3200 and polishing with the same engine returned essentially its start (p0025, 0.876128 -> 0.876133, +0.000005), and a ramp to N=1200/1600 with rebalanced time added only +0.000012 (p0027) and +0.000104 (p0029). These are consistent with a resolution ceiling n

Whether the zero pattern of the winning shape is at its optimum is still open: a threshold sweep that re-zeroed steps below varying quantiles and polished the best candidates moved the zero fraction only from 16.9% to 19.4% and gained +0.000016 (p0030, 0.876128 -> 0.876145). The raw sweep did not reveal a clearly better support pattern, but the polish was cheap and short, so the sparsification que

Adding correlated pairwise coordinate moves (multiplying two indices together, or transferring mass between adjacent pairs) to the engine lets it escape local optima that single-coordinate sweeps cannot, because the winning shapes' gains come from coordinated shifts of neighbouring steps rather than isolated ones. On p0026's one-sided construction (0.878330) a pair-sweep-plus-restructured-stages p

Deepening the perturb-then-engine restart loop on the new one-sided shape still pays: giving coarse N half the restarts and longer per-restart engine slices lifted p0026 (0.878330) to 0.879199 (+0.000869, p0034), confirming the restart loop is not yet saturated after the shape changed.

Whether the one-sided basin is still unsaturated in asymmetry remains open: an explicit monotone tilt sweep on p0026's shape (peak at 0.067) did move the score (0.878330 -> 0.878553, +0.000224, p0031) and shifted f*f's peak to 0.228, but the gain is small and the tilt stage's own contribution versus the trailing restarts is not separated, so it needs a cleaner probe.

Combining the two separately-proven operators on the same state — correlated pair-coordinate sweeps (F18) and the coarse-heavy deep restart loop (F19) — beats either alone: running both inside one restart schedule lifted p0032 (0.879377) to 0.880880 (+0.001503, p0041), the generation's top score, by attacking the correlated-coordinate and restart-depth bottlenecks together rather than one at a tim

Whole-region multiplicative moves — low-frequency cosine modes plus a K~24 control-point block-scaling layer — added to the engine loop give a real gain on the smooth winning shape, lifting p0032 (0.879377) to 0.880093 (+0.000716, p0039). This is the first accepted move class that changes many coordinates coherently at once rather than one coordinate or one pair, confirming that the winning shape'

The pair-sweep + engine method is not state-specific: running p0032's method from p0034's nearby-but-distinct basin (f*f peak 0.440 vs 0.473) lifted it from 0.879199 to 0.880038 (+0.000840, p0038), so the two frontier basins are both live and a small basin ensemble is worth maintaining rather than committing to one base.

Extending correlated moves from pairs to triples (3-way multiplicative sweeps) plus a finer resample and interleaved pair/triple polish between restarts lifted p0032 (0.879377) to 0.880187 (+0.000810, p0042), showing that higher-order coordinate correlations beyond pairs are still a live lever on this shape.

Combining all three separately-proven operator classes — correlated pair sweeps, 3-way triple sweeps, and whole-region cosine-mode/control-point moves — inside one coarse-heavy restart loop gives a real but small gain on the merged-loop frontier state: from p0041 (0.880880) the full compound reached 0.881013 (+0.000133, p0043). The gain is far smaller than the sum of the three operators' individua

The whole-region mode/control-point operator transfers across basins and is the strongest single lever on the p0041 basin: running p0039's mode+ctrl loop unchanged from p0041's construction (f*f peak 0.398) lifted it 0.880880 -> 0.881400 (+0.000520, p0047), the generation's best. This confirms the operator is not tied to p0032's peak-0.514 basin and that broad low-frequency deformations still find

A sqrt-weighted resolution ramp up to N=1600-3000 combined with a pair-sweep stage at the start's native N and smoothing-based restart escapes gave the generation's top score from p0041: 0.880880 -> 0.881543 (+0.000663, p0048). The win comes from giving the smooth profile more degrees of freedom at mid resolution while keeping the pair-sweep and restart machinery active, not from the finest N alon

Reallocating the budget of the sqrt-weighted resolution ramp to the native-N stage is a real lever on the record construction: keeping p0048's helpers but spending ~70% of the budget in a repeating N=200 engine+pair-sweep loop (with small kicks and cycling pair eps) and only a short N=400/800 ramp plus final N=200 pair-polish lifted p0048 (0.881543) to 0.882369 (+0.000826, p0051). The whole-region mode+ctrl operator is still live on the record construction, but only when run at native N: adding a resample-back-to-N=200 stage that runs the mode/ctrl sweeps there (after the first engine stage) lifted p0048 (0.881543) to 0.881708 (+0.000165, p0054). The gain is smaller than the +0.00052 it gave on p0041's basin, consistent with the record optimum being closer to saturated in t
